items.headline: FMRB executive order classified-annex response clock
items.diff_narrative: Monday's first full business day rolls to Tuesday's second, advancing the ten-business-day classified-annex clock from its third to its fourth calendar day and the deadline from T-minus-three to T-minus-two business days against the Friday May 22 expiry. Yesterday's first substantive submission from NIST Director Locascio's office is joined Tuesday by a second submission from the CISA Director's office, lifting the on-record witness count to two of eight with the remaining six confirming draft responses inside the deadline window. Just Security observes that the two-of-eight pace at this point in the cycle matches the steeper response cadence the eight-witness slate had targeted. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee's parallel joint-resolution draft converts from Monday's markup-scheduling decision into a Tuesday-morning posted markup notice, the first formal House-track movement on the FMRB track since the order's signing window opened.

items.headline: Cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter at fifteen jurisdictions
items.diff_narrative: The fifteen-named-candidate count plus the originating UK and EU holds steady from Monday to Tuesday, but the schema-comment metric and the calendar both advance. OECD GENAI secretariat-reported member-state submissions on the finalized attestation field schema move from past two-thirds of the named candidate cohort to past three-quarters as the business week's second day clears, with the plenary target stepping from roughly T-minus-three weeks to T-minus-two weeks against the June 2-6 adoption window, and the secretariat publishes a Tuesday calendar item placing the schema-comment close at the end of next week. Qatar's 270-day national-consultation window rolls from its first full week into its second, and the United States recognition gap continues to hold open with the FMRB executive order — now at classified-annex day four — still the cited closure instrument.

items.headline: n8n CVE-2026-21858 exposure taper before May 21 deadline
items.diff_narrative: The day-eighteen Monday scan rolls to day-nineteen Tuesday with the federal-civilian remediation deadline stepping from T-minus-three to T-minus-two business days. The weekday descent extends rather than steepens: internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances fall from roughly 1,640 to roughly 1,395, the residual unpatched long-tail share eases from about 12 percent to about 10 percent, the US cohort eases from roughly 510 to roughly 410 and India from roughly 270 to roughly 215, and Censys exploitation telemetry holds flat at 1.7x baseline — consistent with commodity-tier volume settling rather than ramping ahead of the deadline. The CISA federal-civilian operational directive that published Monday morning moves from publication to its first full operating day with federal-civilian operators reporting incremental remediation completions against the catalogued patterns.

items.headline: MCP-server attack-surface telemetry holds above 90 percent
items.diff_narrative: Monday's weekday cadence carries into Tuesday's business-week second day with each consecutive-day counter ticking up one. The credential-extraction median holds at 5 minutes for an eighth consecutive day (from a seventh) with the unprotected-versus-protected gap still near 67x, and Defender-for-Cloud quarantine on net-new MCP servers ticks from 48 percent to 49 percent — a ninth consecutive day of expansion (from an eighth). Cisco-Astrix identity-gateway tenancy edges from roughly 2,420 to roughly 2,455 enterprise tenants and Akamai SkyAtlas MCP-firewall from roughly 1,390 to roughly 1,410, with CrowdStrike Falcon for Agentic AI holding its 91-percent managed-visibility composition and the total exposed-server estimate easing from roughly 9,050 to roughly 8,960 as weekday provisioning continues.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS follow-through after Monday's first re-rating session
items.diff_narrative: Monday's first re-rating session for the four-day consolidation base rolls to Tuesday's follow-through session with the May 21 Alphabet analyst day stepping from T-minus-three to T-minus-two calendar days. The five-desk analyst spread carries unchanged into the second trading day inside the same roughly $185-to-$235 band, with Morgan Stanley's upside-scenario probability nudging from 41 percent to 42 percent, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging from roughly 37 percent to roughly 38 percent of float as desks added incremental long exposure, and the Saudi PIF contingent-secondary discussion moving from inside its 10-21 day execution window into the second week of that window. The desk preview cohort treats Tuesday as the first session in the analyst-day run-up where directional positioning typically firms ahead of a Mag-7 print catalyst.

items.headline: Mag-7 print-cycle preview ahead of the May 21 Alphabet analyst day
items.diff_narrative: The Alphabet analyst day steps from Monday's T-minus-three to Tuesday's T-minus-two calendar days, and the run-up window enters its second session. The six-desk preview cohort nudges the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability from 88 percent to 89 percent — a further one-point uptick — with the Friday SEC Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter still the settled disclosure-precedent input and the cohort now treating Tuesday's Cerebras follow-through as a coincident input rather than a separate catalyst. On the AI-accelerator IPO track, Tenstorrent's first-round comment-letter response advances from Monday's filed-at-the-11-business-day-mark status to a 12-business-day mark inside the staff-review interval ahead of a likely second-round letter, with the early-August public-filing target and SambaNova's six-bookrunner roster both unchanged.

items.headline: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 registry growth and gated-tenant signings
items.diff_narrative: Day eleven rolls to day twelve with the second-week growth normalization extending — published skills rise from roughly 31,050 to roughly 32,800 (+5.6 percent, a sixth consecutive sub-7-percent reading), skill installs from roughly 2.74M to roughly 2.86M, and auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills from 68 to 71. The gated-tenant cohort extends Monday's resumed weekday cadence: two further enterprise customers join to lift the Mythos-Preview count from 66 to 68, with the new entrants in the Indo-Pacific allied public-sector tier (vs Monday's Continental European tier). The verification harness's cross-tenant compositional safety check continues to hold under 55 seconds across all 68 tenants, and now folds in Monday's training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification as an optional verification step alongside the standard audit.

items.headline: Mistral AI Workflows adds a ninth central-government reference
items.diff_narrative: Monday's eighth central-government reference (Netherlands Belastingdienst) rolls to Tuesday's ninth as Sweden Skatteverket joins, the second fresh central-government estate selection of the business week. Paid Workflows tenancy edges from roughly 401 to roughly 408 enterprise customers and daily executions from roughly 7.4M to roughly 7.5M. The five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix holds its first-week-of-June general-availability target, and the conformance test suite holds green across all five vendors for a second consecutive weekday with no schema-drift regression — and now includes the training-surface checkpoint-provenance check folded in from Monday's arxiv extension.

items.headline: OpenAI per-org agent registry extends to a tenth Indo-Pacific region
items.diff_narrative: Monday's nine-region Indo-Pacific GA footprint rolls to Tuesday's tenth region as Thailand joins (after Malaysia on Monday), the second regional extension of the business week. GA-cohort tenancy edges from roughly 351 to roughly 358 enterprise customers, and OpenAI ships a Codex CLI v3.1.6 point release — one minor patch on top of Monday's v3.1.5 — continuing the consolidation of the four-tier-and-sub-tier-plus-nested-dependency-resolution client-side mitigation surface ahead of the early-June cross-orchestrator interop matrix GA target. The cohort reads the Thailand addition as continuing to track the fifteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter rather than expand ahead of it, and flags the OECD plenary's T-minus-two-week mark as the next inflection point for whether the footprint widens beyond fifteen.

items.headline: Unsloth follow-up tightens Monday's new MoE router-only LoRA path
items.diff_narrative: Monday's feature update — a faster Mixture-of-Experts router-only LoRA path delivering roughly a 4 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on the DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe — gets a Tuesday follow-up tightening: a router-attention all-reduce schedule refinement on top of the reworked expert-gradient bucketing layout lands a further roughly 0.6 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on the same single-node octa-Hopper run. The optional training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification step from Monday's arxiv 2605.07588 paper is now wired directly into the router-only training driver. The DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe draws a tenth Hacker News reproduction (from a ninth) — a dual-RTX 5090 consumer workstation hits roughly 5.0 percent peak combined VRAM on the refined path, down from Monday's roughly 5.5 percent — and a contributor opens a pull request porting the new MoE path to the Qwen3 MoE 60B class.

items.headline: vLLM v0.11.4 stable holds into its first full operating day
items.diff_narrative: Monday's published v0.11.4 stable cut rolls to its first full operating day on Tuesday. The Yotta Labs throughput gap narrows from roughly 2.2 percent to roughly 2.0 percent — about 19,180 tok/s on v0.11.4 stable versus about 19,560 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9, the tightest reading of the benchmark cycle — with Cloudflare Infire holding L40S edge-tier parity at 1.00x into the second day post-stable. The vLLM Blog opens a v0.11.5 development branch that adds the optional training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification hook from Monday's arxiv 2605.07588 paper as a paving step on top of the existing five-surface mitigation set, and the serving-stack cohort treats Tuesday as the first day the stable tag plus the Monday CISA federal-civilian operational directive can be cited together as a stable reference for the upstream framework cohort.

items.headline: Tenstorrent Galaxy rack shipments extend the weekday cadence
items.diff_narrative: Monday's seventh-wave weekday cadence carries into Tuesday with a fresh batch lifting the cumulative count from roughly 177 to roughly 187 racks against the 280-rack first-half target — about 67 percent fulfilled (up from about 63 percent, a four-point uptick). Additions span CoreWeave and Lambda Labs in North America plus a second Asia-Pacific increment to Yotta Labs India and a small second re-up to the European sovereign-cloud cohort, adding UpCloud Finland and Telefonica Tech Spain on top of Monday's OVHcloud France and Hetzner Online Germany. AMD's Helios plus MI450 commitment book advances from near 10.4GW to near 10.55GW with a fresh weekday sovereign-cloud commitment — the second new commitment of the business week — and the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 holds its early-August public-filing target.

items.headline: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 activates a ninth Fremont cohort
items.diff_narrative: Monday's eighth cohort rolls to Tuesday's ninth: a fresh cohort of roughly twelve units comes online, lifting the active count from 96 to 108 of the disclosed 240-unit allocation — 45 percent reached (up from 40 percent) — with cycle-time still holding at the roughly 1.03x human-baseline envelope. The ninth cohort enters the Fremont automotive line on the same multi-station sealed parts-transfer chain that has now become the standard cohort-onboarding workflow, with cross-cell coordination on the eighth-cohort line continuing without incident through its first day-plus operating window. The Stellantis Detroit (June 8) and Volkswagen Wolfsburg (June 22) activation dates hold, and Standard Bots notes that the roughly 12-unit weekday cadence would complete the disclosed allocation inside June if the pattern holds.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics Atlas clears 120-hour milestone, runs toward 144-hour
items.diff_narrative: BMW Group's Spartanburg 30-unit Atlas pilot clears Monday's first North American 120-hour continuous-operation milestone and now runs toward a first North American 144-hour milestone on the under-body conveyor task with zero MTBF-impacting incidents. Volkswagen Wolfsburg's Atlas pilot edges from roughly 84 to roughly 88 units on the body-shop welding-jig material-handoff task as the second weekday shift carries Monday's expansion. The humanoid league-table OEM-adopter roster of six now has a flagged seventh — Mercedes-Benz Sindelfingen — entering due-diligence on a 25-unit pilot scope with no commitment yet. Hyundai Metaplant's Dangjin rolling-mill cycle-time improvement holds near 5.1 percent for an eighth consecutive within-band day (from a seventh), with the policy-distillation pipeline still running on the Tenstorrent Galaxy plus Unsloth router-only stack.

items.headline: Tuesday arxiv tenant-policy-attestation paper extends loader verification to the deployment gate
items.diff_narrative: A fresh Tuesday arxiv release, 2605.07735, opens the business week's second research day by extending the loader-verification line one further surface — from Monday's training-pipeline checkpoint-provenance extension to a tenant-policy-attestation surface. Positioned as a third extension of the consolidated 2605.07241 framework after its 2605.07412 empirical companion and Monday's 2605.07588 training-surface extension rather than a fresh model, it formalizes how the training-surface provenance chain composes with a tenant-policy-attestation manifest covering the fifteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter's tenant-policy field schemas, giving a single end-to-end signed reference from training-run checkpoint through agent-loader through tenant-policy gate with only marginal additional overhead. Simon Willison characterizes it as the loader-verification line reaching its third documented extension within the May 16-19 four-day cluster, with the four papers now forming a unified reference set the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment commitment can cite as a single coherent surface.
